newsitem.title: KENYA: FOCUS - Kenya shilling up a little as dollars sold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Kenya shilling up a little as dollars sold.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened marginally against the dollar on Friday as dollars were sold in profit-making a day after the shilling slumped to a record low.
At 12:30 p.m. (0930 GMT) on Friday, the shilling was trading at a commercial mean rate of 68.96 against the dollar compared with its opening rate of 70.26 -- a 1.85 percent gain.
Commercial bank dealers said it was too early to declare an end to the shilling's slide since the IMF halted a key loan package last week.
They said the foreign exchange market was uneasy because of a national strike on Friday called by an opposition-backed alliance demanding constitutional reforms from President Daniel Arap Moi.
"The market is very thin today because most people did not turn up to trade," said a dealer.
"People are now selling dollars because they've seen there is very little business. Most of them were in long dollar positions," a senior dealer told Reuters.

The movement on Friday brought the shilling's total loss against the dollar since news of the IMF decision to 15.90 percent compared with a 18.08 percent loss at Thursday's close after the shilling sunk to a new official record low of 70.26.
The centre of Nairobi was calm on Friday but some shops and offices were closed because of fears of violence during the one-day national strike called by some opposition leaders.
In a bid to calm the turbulent market on Thursday, Finance minister Musalia Mudavadi said the government was considering talks with the IMF on securing a second year of the three-year loan package.
But in another blow to the government, an International Monetary Fund spokesman said Kenya must move against corruption before any talks to revive the IMF loan halted on Thursday last week.
